systematic_issues:
1) CONFIRMED, and it is the dominant defect in this batch: grade-3 cutoffs were anchored to a fraction of a scale's numeric range, not to what the scale's text says the value means. The rows' own notes expose the rule - "mapping 0-<1=>0, 1-<3=>1, 3-<5=>2, >=5=>3" (acute tables) and "0-<1=>0, 1-<3=>2, >=3=>3" (8-week tables) - applied identically to three batteries that are NOT interchangeable: (a) US10968453B2's rat FOB, whose sub-score is only "whether the rat exhibits normal function in the region of interest (0) or does not (1)" over seven body regions - no severity ladder, no death, no paralysis term at any score; (b) US9605263B2 / US9683235B2's rat score, whose sub-score is explicitly "0 if the body part was moving or 1 if the body part was paralyzed" - so here even a mid-range value denotes paralysis; (c) the 7-criterion mouse battery, an ordered severity ladder in which grade-3 meaning starts at 6 ("the mouse responded to a tail pinch" failed) and 7 adds "regular breathing" failed. The same number - say 6.0 - therefore means "six regions abnormal" (grade 2) in one patent and "six body parts paralyzed" (grade 3) in another. Any grade-3 row in the wider dataset whose neurotox_grade came from a >=5-of-7 or >=3-of-7 rule should be re-derived from the cited patent's own scale text.
2) CONFIRMED: US9605263B2 Table 15's "Score 8 weeks after injection" is an animal-loss readout, not a persisting-deficit score. 89 of the 92 compound rows sit exactly on the 7*k/4 grid for 4-mouse groups (only 0.0, 1.8, 3.5, 5.3, 7.0 occur, with three off-grid exceptions: 801304 4.8, 802467 1.3, 802470 1.5); all 46 zero-score rows carry unasterisked 4-mouse AIF1/GFAP while 44 of 46 nonzero rows carry asterisked ("average of 1-3 mice") or N.D. values - the two exceptions being exactly two of the three off-grid rows; and all eight rows scoring 7.0 have N.D. in all four RT-PCR columns. At 8 weeks each mouse scored 0 or the full 7, so the group mean counts dead animals. The same signature is present in the rat Table 16 (nonzero 8-week scores 3.5 / 2.3 / 1.8 are precisely the asterisked "average of 2-3 mice" rows). Every 8-week-score row sourced from this patent family needs re-labelling as mortality; the grade happens to remain 3, but the readout_name, readout_category and any dose-response modelling built on these numbers are wrong.
3) CONFIRMED: the US9605263B2 mouse rows assert a vehicle comparator the patent does not contain. All 24 mouse rows from Tables 7, 8 and 15 carry effect_vs_control "X_vs_0_PBS" and several carry notes saying "PBS controls score 0", but Examples 2, 3 and 12 dose ASO groups only, and the single "Saline treated ... generally receive a score of 0" sentence in this patent is in Example 13 and is about RATS. The sentence does exist for mice in US10968453B2 Example 18 and US9683235B2 Example 20, which is almost certainly where it was imported from - a cross-patent contamination pattern worth grepping for elsewhere in the patents lane.
4) Not a defect but worth recording: reversibility is "not_assessed" on the acute rat rows even where the same patent prints a paired 8-week reading that shows recovery (US10968453B2 Table 67: ISIS 666870 5.8 at 3 h vs 0.8 at 8 weeks) or 8-week glial markers proving the animals survived (Table 65, e.g. ISIS 666867 IBA1 132% / GFAP 112% of control). Those paired columns are free evidence for the reversibility field and for keeping acute scores out of grade 3.
